faqs.question: How is the price of a piece calculated?
faqs.answer: Jewellery prices are built from the metal rate for the piece's purity multiplied by its net weight, plus making charges, stone charges (where applicable) and any other charges. GST is then applied and any offer is deducted. Every product page shows this breakdown.

faqs.question: Why can the price of a piece change?
faqs.answer: Gold and silver rates move with the market. Prices on the website are updated from our pricing system, and the final price is confirmed when you place your order.

faqs.question: What is the difference between 22KT and 18KT gold?
faqs.answer: 22KT gold contains 91.6% pure gold and has a rich, warm colour. 18KT gold contains 75% pure gold; the added alloy makes it harder, which is why it is often used for diamond and gemstone settings.

faqs.question: Which payment methods can I use?
faqs.answer: Payments are processed through our secure payment gateway. The methods available to you are shown at checkout.

faqs.question: How do I track my order?
faqs.answer: Sign in and open My Account → Orders to see the live status of every order, from confirmation through to delivery.

faqs.question: How long will delivery take?
faqs.answer: Delivery timelines depend on the piece and your location. They are confirmed with your order — please see our Shipping Policy for details.

faqs.question: Can I return or exchange a piece?
faqs.answer: Please refer to our Returns & Refund Policy for eligibility and the process. Our team is happy to help with any questions.

faqs.question: Can you make a custom piece for me?
faqs.answer: Yes. Share your idea through the Custom Jewellery page or on WhatsApp — include reference images, preferred metal and budget. Our team will contact you to discuss design, feasibility and timelines.

faqs.question: How do I find my ring or bangle size?
faqs.answer: Choose from the sizes listed on the product page. If you are unsure, contact us on WhatsApp and we will guide you through measuring at home.

faqs.question: How should I care for my jewellery?
faqs.answer: Store pieces separately in a soft pouch, keep them away from perfume and chemicals, and wipe gently with a soft cloth after wearing. Silver can be brightened with a silver polishing cloth.

blog.title: How jewellery prices are calculated
blog.excerpt: Metal rate, purity, weight, making charges and GST — a clear guide to reading a jewellery price.

coverImage.alt: Gold necklace with intricate bead detailing on velvet

content.text: Unlike most products, the price of gold and silver jewellery is built from several transparent components. Understanding them helps you compare pieces with confidence.
1. Metal value
The metal value is the rate for the piece's purity multiplied by its net weight — the weight of the metal alone, excluding stones or beads.
2. Making charges
Making charges reflect the design and craftsmanship involved. They may be expressed per gram, as a percentage of the metal value, or as a fixed amount.
3. Stone and other charges
Diamonds, gemstones, pearls or beads are priced separately. Other charges can include specific finishing or stringing work.
4. GST and offers
GST is applied to the taxable value. Where an offer applies, the discount is shown clearly in the breakdown.
A clear price is the foundation of a confident purchase.

items: Compare net weight, not only gross weight.
Look at making charges alongside the design.
Confirm the final price at checkout.

blog.title: 22KT vs 18KT gold: choosing the right purity
blog.excerpt: Colour, durability and design — how purity shapes the jewellery you choose.

coverImage.alt: Detail of gold jewellery worn with a red and gold sari

content.text: Purity describes how much pure gold an alloy contains. It affects colour, hardness and the kind of designs a piece can support.
22KT gold
22KT gold is 91.6% pure gold. Its deep yellow tone is traditional in Indian jewellery, and it is ideal for bangles, chains and ceremonial pieces.
18KT gold
18KT gold is 75% pure gold. The higher proportion of alloy makes it harder, so it holds diamonds and gemstones securely and suits fine, contemporary designs.

items: Choose 22KT for rich colour and traditional designs.
Choose 18KT for stone-set and delicate pieces.
Both are priced by the rate for their specific purity.

blog.title: Caring for sterling silver
blog.excerpt: Simple habits that keep your silver bright for years.

coverImage.alt: Silver chain bracelets reflected on a mirror

content.text: 925 sterling silver is 92.5% pure silver. Like all silver, it can tarnish naturally when exposed to air and moisture — the good news is that it is easy to care for.
Everyday care

items: Put jewellery on after perfume and lotions.
Wipe with a soft cloth after wearing.
Store in a sealed pouch to slow tarnishing.

content.text: Restoring shine
A silver polishing cloth restores brightness gently. For pieces with stones or oxidised detailing, avoid dips and harsh cleaners.

blog.title: The art of layering necklaces
blog.excerpt: Proportion, length and texture — how to build a layered look that feels effortless.

coverImage.alt: Woman wearing a fine gold necklace

content.text: Layering lets you tell a personal story through jewellery. The secret is contrast with a common thread.
Vary the lengths
Leave around 5cm between each layer so every piece has room to be seen.
Mix textures, keep one tone
Pair a fine box chain with a rope chain or a pendant in the same metal for a cohesive look.

image.alt: Layered gold necklace on white fabric

content.caption: A pre-layered necklace keeps strands from tangling.

blog.title: Planning your bridal jewellery
blog.excerpt: A calm, step-by-step approach to choosing jewellery for every wedding function.

coverImage.alt: Bride in a wedding sari looking downward

content.text: Bridal jewellery is often the most meaningful purchase you will make. A little planning makes the experience joyful rather than overwhelming.
Start with your outfits
Neckline, colour and embroidery guide which necklace shapes and metals will work best for each function.
Balance heirloom and everyday
Alongside statement sets, choose a few pieces — like a mangalsutra, fine chain or bangles — that you will wear long after the celebrations.
Personalise
Custom jewellery allows you to add initials, dates or family motifs. Allow time for design discussion and confirmation.
